cards.explanation: The answer is his own life. Jesus says, "…yes, even his own life—he cannot be My disciple." (Luke 14:26) The list starts with the people closest to a person and then lands on the person himself. I think that's the part that makes you sit up straight, friends.

The answer is his cross. Jesus says, "And whoever does not carry his cross and follow Me cannot be My disciple." (Luke 14:27) Carrying and following go together in that one sentence, so a disciple doesn't get to pick the easier half. I'd pick the easier half every time, and I'm saying it out loud so nobody else has to.

The answer is count the cost. Jesus says the builder will "…first sit down and count the cost to see if he has the resources to complete it?" (Luke 14:28) Sit down first, then count. I wish I had done that before I tried to stamp a hundred cookies with one bowl of dough, friends.

The answer is that they ridicule him. Jesus says, "…everyone who sees it will ridicule him…" (Luke 14:29) Everyone who sees it, not just one or two people. The builder laid the foundation and couldn't finish, and I'd say that's rough on him.

The answer is twenty thousand. Jesus pictures the king with ten thousand men facing "…the one coming against him with twenty thousand?" (Luke 14:31) That's two soldiers for every one of his. Sitting down to think first sounds pretty smart to me, bakers.

The answer is peace. The king "…will send a delegation while the other king is still far off, to ask for terms of peace." (Luke 14:32) He does it while the other king is still far off, not after the armies are in his face. A smart move, I'd say, friends.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "In the same way, any one of you who does not give up everything he has cannot be My disciple." (Luke 14:33) He took the builder and the king and tied them straight to the crowd. The words "In the same way…" are the hinge between those two pictures and the people in front of Him, bakers.

The answer is False. Jesus says the salt "…is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile, and it is thrown out." (Luke 14:35) It isn't fit for either place, so it gets thrown out. That's a hard fall for something Jesus just called good, friends.
